title: Homepage
lead: Manage independent Homepage publications with scheduled selection, public document sources and shared raw-data Mustache.

sections.title: Create a Homepage draft
steps: Open Homepage → New Homepage. Enter a name and description and choose HTML/Mustache or a published plugin document as the content source.

For HTML, write static content in the shared Visual editor or use Code for semantic HTML and protected Mustache structures. Select existing public media locally or enter allowed remote URLs; upload new files in Images first.
For a plugin document, select an available published Page or Blog article. Save draft and inspect Preview. Saving a draft does not replace the published snapshot.

sections.title: Publish, schedule and select a Homepage
steps: Save the draft, set the intended publication time and choose Publish / schedule. Review UTC versus browser-local date entry before confirming.
Use Overview to inspect enabled publications. The newest due valid snapshot becomes effective; future snapshots wait until their date. Global Settings supplies Homepage metadata.
Deactivate a publication to allow the preceding valid one to take over. The protected legacy-home baseline cannot be removed. Missing/unpublished document sources do not expose drafts.

sections.title: Legacy template-owned components
steps: In the legacy native editor only, Insert component discovers enabled services, typed parameters and template-owned presentations. Its colon markers remain compatible with earlier content. New HTML mode instead uses explicit data bindings and the variable/loop syntax documented below.
Create reusable widgets and ordered sets in Widgets. Their keys do not need template positions. The template still controls every component format.

sections.title: Publication catalog and raw data
steps: Create named homepages in Overview / New homepage. Save draft never changes the published snapshot. Publish / schedule copies the saved content to a separate snapshot. Dates are exact UTC seconds; the editor also offers browser-local entry. At request time the newest due enabled snapshot wins, with immutable ID as a deterministic tie-breaker. Future snapshots do not replace the currently effective homepage early. Deactivation/removal returns to the next valid enabled publication. The protected legacy-home baseline preserves the native original homepage and cannot be removed. No cron or render-time writes are required.

HTML mode accepts semantic HTML, escaped variables, # sections/loops, ^ inverted sections and comments. Add multiple plugin/service bindings, give each a unique alias and insert snippets manually. Plugin results are plain JSON, never HTML or executable helpers. Source mode references a currently published Page or Blog article by stable ID; a missing/unpublished/disabled source falls back to the preceding valid homepage. Source body excludes its own site frame. Metadata always comes from global settings. Preview is authenticated and noindex. Trash recovery does not automatically activate content.

sections.title: Editable native Homepage
steps: The content-source selector contains HTML/Mustache and plugin documents only. An installed template can declare a homepageMarkup adapter to convert its native sections to editable HTML. Existing legacy catalogs and private history stay readable; conversion is never a public rendering write.

Declared markupFragments retain live contact forms and plugin integrations without saving rendered tokens or provider snapshots. Insert {{template:fragment id="contact"}} for a registered public fragment; {{cms.base}} keeps local links portable. Private previews show inert fragment labels. See docs/homepage-conversion.md for adapter and CAS migration contracts.

sections.title: Recover publications and legacy drafts
steps: Open History to inspect catalog revisions and access Legacy drafts when older working copies exist. Restore only the intended revision.
Move an ordinary publication to Trash when no longer needed; use the final Trash item to recover it. Recovery does not automatically activate it.
Review and publish recovered content explicitly. Disabling the plugin preserves the published website; private drafts, history and trash are excluded from exports.
